gaps: Gives no guidance at all for redox measurement with an ORP sensor on a multiparameter sonde — the exact configuration a rover carries. Section 6.5.1 states outright that the report does not cover it, so no calibration interval, no drift tolerance, and no maintenance schedule for a sonde ORP sensor exists anywhere in this document.

States no acceptable ORP/Eh range or threshold for any natural water type: no expected mV window for oxic surface water, for anoxic ground water, or for stream monitoring, and no action level at which a reading should be rejected.

Gives no ORP calibration frequency in the sense a continuous-monitoring program needs (before each field trip, and before/after field use, is the only cadence stated); nothing on how often a deployed sensor must be re-checked, nor on allowable drift per day of deployment.

Provides no conversion or offset table for reporting ORP as raw sensor millivolts rather than Eh — the document assumes the operator adds a reference half-cell potential by hand and reports Eh, and never addresses instruments that report ORP directly.

Half-cell table 6.5-2 stops at 40 degrees Celsius and starts at 10 degrees Celsius, so no reference potential is given for water below 10 or above 40 degrees C; the only remedy offered is interpolation, which cannot extrapolate.

Gives no accuracy or precision specification for the Eh measurement itself (only agreement criteria: plus or minus 5 mV against ZoBell's, about 10 mV between duplicate field readings). There is no stated method detection limit or uncertainty budget.
Says nothing about ORP sensor fouling in continuous deployment (biofouling, sediment), cleaning intervals for a deployed sensor, or how a fouled ORP reading manifests in a time series.
Names no field data-quality codes, qualifiers, or flags for rejecting an unstable Eh record beyond 'assume a single quantitative value is not possible'.

Contains no cross-metric interpretation guidance: no Eh-pH stability diagram, no rule relating an ORP reading to dissolved-oxygen concentration, and no numeric ORP value associated with the onset of anoxia.
summary.notes:
Corpus/OCR damage: this document's text file contains NUL bytes and other C0 control characters, all of them inside Table 6.5-1 (equipment and supplies). That table was extracted through a shifted font encoding — every character sits 0x20 below its true value (T stored as '4', E as '%', space as NUL, '.' as 0x0e), so the table reads as 'ILLIVOLT METER OR P( METER...' in the corpus. It is decodable by hand (it resolves to 'millivolt meter or pH meter with millivolt reading capability... 0.1 mV sensitivity; scale to at least +/-1,400 mV; BNC connector... deionized water (maximum conductivity of 1.0 uS/cm)'), but no retrieval arm will ever match a plain-text query against it and no fixture should be built on it. Only one low-specificity claim (orp-table651-tubing-oxygen-01) is recorded from it, quoting the one control-character-free span in the table.
Table 6.5-2 arrives with its data rows intact but its COLUMN HEADERS PRINTED AFTER THE TABLE BODY: the numeric rows (10 through 40 degrees C) appear first, then the footnotes, then the header block ('Calomel', 'Orion 96-78 combination electrode', 'Temp o C', '3 M KCl', '3.5 M KCl', 'Saturated KCl', ... 'Silver:silver chloride'). Column-to-value mapping is therefore recoverable only by reading the header block in order and matching it to the eight numeric columns; a fixture asking 'what is the Ag:AgCl saturated-KCl half-cell potential at 25 C' is answerable from this chunk but only by a reader who reconstructs that ordering. Values are in volts, not millivolts.
Table 6.5-3 (Eh of ZoBell's vs temperature) survives intact and is the cleanest numeric table in the document, but it is laid out in two side-by-side column pairs on one line (e.g. '10\t467\t26\t428' means 467 mV at 10 C and 428 mV at 26 C). A naive reader could mis-parse the third column as an Eh value. It is also duplicated in full in chunk 7's 400-character overlap; claims are attributed to chunk 6 where it originates.
Table 6.5-4 (troubleshooting) survives with symptom and corrective-action columns interleaved, so symptoms ('Excessive drift', 'Erratic performance') sit on the same lines as unrelated corrective actions.
Internal tension worth knowing: chunk 5 says 'Eh equipment must be tested ... before making field measurements' and then immediately says 'In general, field testing with ZoBell's is not required' — these are reconcilable (lab test required, field test optional) but read as contradictory if either sentence is retrieved alone.
Chunk 15 is pure bibliography and yields no extractable claim; chunks 14 and 16 are mostly bibliography. Chunk 0 opens mid-list-of-tables (document front matter).
The document's own framing is a strong negative: it says redox measurement 'is not recommended in general' and that a single Eh value 'generally does not represent the system'. Any fixture that treats this manual as endorsing routine ORP monitoring will be wrong.
